lit:
Round-1 and round-2 literature (sources opened and quoted by reviewers):
- arXiv:2605.12822 proves: r|a_i => unimodal (Cor 4.3); k=1 iff (Prop 5.3); k=2,r=2 iff (Prop 4.5).
- Unrefereed AI-assisted GitHub notes (Sept 2026): ProveIt (sufficiency b<=1+F for all r via centered peeling; necessary bound b<=1+floor(D/r); r=2 and r=3 complete criteria, the r=3 one equal to b<=1+F+2floor(t/6); 'open for k<=3 with r>=4'); AI-Has-Taste (k=2 iff for every r); omega-institute (Lean refutation of the r<=3 necessity clause via (1+q)^6(1+q^3)).
- Handelman, arXiv:1102.2961: (1+x)^m(1+x^k) is unimodal iff log-concave iff m >= k^2-3.
- Not found in any source: exact principal-value criterion; parity of the excess; closed form on the whole flat domain (only special cases known); necessity for k=3, r>=4; eventual residue determination; Conjecture S2; non-monotonicity in b; aggregate non-existence.
Round-3 step 0 (48 queries; no source states any round-2 claim in general form): class-pair/thread criterion, parity/closure, S2 shape, large-part stabilization, all-equal family: 文献连线 only to special cases (ProveIt Lemma 4.1 tail residue-mass differences for n>=S-r+2; AHT k=2; ProveIt r=2, r=3; Handelman b=2; ProveIt Cor 3.3 sufficient-direction residue reduction, 'not an assertion that residue reduction preserves unimodality in both directions'). Not found: cyclic unimodality of class sums (contrast: Krason-Milewski arXiv:1905.11815 Example 4.8, residue-class sums of a Gaussian polynomial 80,75,78,76,78,75 are NOT cyclically unimodal), three-middle closed form, the r=8595 pair-local counterexample. Adjacent: Xin-Zhong arXiv:1912.01829 (parity-unimodality <=> (1+q)C(q) unimodal); Abdallah-McDaniel ALCO 8(2) 2025 Thm 1.3 ([m]_t[m]_{t^2} unimodal iff m even); Dolgopyat-Hafouta arXiv:2011.14852 (Edgeworth expansions with mod-h obstructions).
known:
(Notation: F = sum floor(a_i/r), D = sum(a_i-1), Gamma_t = residue-class-t sum of coefficients of A=prod[a_i]_q mod r, mu = least t in [0,r-1] with Gamma_t>=...>=Gamma_{r-1}, T6 = 1+floor((D+1-2mu)/r), U = {b: P unimodal}; a residue in [2,r-2] is 'middle'.)
- C43: r | a_i for some i => unimodal for all b.
- T1: b <= 1+F => unimodal (all r, k).
- T6 (Thm C): r divides no a_i and unimodal => b <= T6. Lemma 7: E6 = T6-1-F is always even and >= 0.
- Thm A (exact criterion): with h = two-sided (principal-value) expansion coefficients of A(q)/[r]_q and K = D+1-r(b+1): P unimodal iff h_m <= h_{K-m} for all integers 1-rb <= m < K/2. Equivalent forms: d_u = coefficients of A(q)(1-q)/(1-q^r), tau = r-periodic tail; or g = coefficients of A(q)/[r]_q: unimodal iff g_i >= g_{i-rb} for 0<=i<=floor(N/2).
- Thm E: if at most two a_i have a middle residue (always for r<=3): P unimodal iff b <= T6. (r=3: b<=1+F+2floor(S/6), S=#{a_i=2 mod 3}; r=2: b<=1+F.)
- Thm D: at most three a_i with residue outside {0,1} => unimodal iff b <= 1+F.
- Thm B (peeling): [a]_q[b]_{q^r} = [a+r(b-1)]_q + q^r[a-r]_q[b-1]_{q^r}; U(a+r e_i) contains {1} ∪ (1+U(a)). B4: if all a_i >= L0(r, residues), U = [1,F] ∪ (F + U_inf(r, residue vector)), U_inf finite, computable from 1/((1-q)^{k-1}(1-q^r)) and tau.
- T7: no function of (r,k,b,residue multiset,F,D) decides unimodality (r=6,b=4: a=(2,3,4,4,4,4,4,8) unimodal, a'=(2,2,3,4,4,4,4,10) not).
- N1: U need not be an interval (r=6, a=(2,3,3,4,4,4,5): U={1,3}).
- Round-2 results (all proved and refereed unless marked). You may read the refereed round-2 proof files: /tmp/claude-0/qu/explore2/R2E1/proof_S2_partial.txt, R2E2/proof_S2_reduction.txt, R2E3/proof_S2_partial.txt, R2E5/proofs.txt, R2E6/proof_excess_asymptotics.txt, R2E7/proofs.txt, R2E8/proof_three_middle.txt (all under /tmp/claude-0/qu/explore2/), but not other files there.
- T9 thread criterion (R2E1): S2(i) [b in U, b == F (mod 2) => b+1 in U]; max U == 1+F (mod 2) when r divides no a_i; step-2 closure [b in U, b>=3 => b-2 in U]; U finite iff r divides no a_i.
- T10 (R2E2): S2 follows from three finite residue-level conditions TP_rho, E_rho, O_rho on the residue instance rho (part sizes never matter, by lifting). Proof file /tmp/claude-0/qu/explore2/R2E2/proof_S2_reduction.txt (you may read it). Statement: let r divide no a_i, rho = residue multiset, sigma = sum(rho_i-1), d = coefficients of A(1-q)/(1-q^r), tau = residue-class sums of (1-q)A, Q_u = d_u - tau_{u mod r}, ND(K): Q_{K-x} >= d_x for all x with K-r <= 2x < K, mu*_inf = max{u: f_u < tau_u} with f = coefficients of 1/((1-q)^{k-1}(1-q^r)); (TP) every z with Q^rho_z<0 has floor((sigma+1-2z)/r) even; (E) ND_rho(K) for all K == sigma+1 mod 2r with 2mu*_inf <= K <= sigma+1-2r; (O) ND_rho(K) for all K == sigma+1+r mod 2r with 2mu*_inf+3r <= K <= sigma+1-2r. Certificate verified for 3,154,273 residue multisets (r<=30). The k-independent strong version fails for 25,737/1,547,599 long rho.
- T11 (R2E3): U = [1,sigma] u {sigma+2, ..., tau*-2}, sigma == tau* == 1+F (mod 2); S2 <=> tau* <= sigma+4. Lemma 7 (PROVED): the residue-class sums Gamma_t of prod[a_i]_q are cyclically unimodal on Z/r, peaked at S/2 (S = D).
- T12 (R2E5): window lemma; all-equal a=[nr+s]^k (middle s): U = [1,kn+1] u (kn+1+E_inf) for n>=1, 4<=r<=30, 3<=k<=60; E_inf = {odd e<=E_odd} u {even e<=E_even}, E_odd<E_even (all r>=4).
- T13 (R2E6): E = B*-1-F satisfies |E - (c k - ln k/(r lambda))| <= C2 for fixed r and residue proportions with positive middle mass, a_min large; c = (sigma1-2theta*)/r, theta* root of (1+t)ln(1+t)-t ln t = L, L = max_j sum_s p_s ln|sin(pi j s/r)/sin(pi j/r)|, lambda = ln(1+1/theta*), sigma1 = sum p_s(s-1); 0<c<sigma1/r.
- T14 (R2E7): explicit L0 = max(1, floor((S-k+3-r)/2)) (S = sum(a_i-1)) suffices for the large-part regime (not sharp); U(a) c [1,F+1] u (F+U_inf); U_inf has two-chain structure; U_inf c [1,T6-F]. FALSE: 'U_inf has one of three shapes [1,T],[1,T]-{T-1},[1,T-2]' (r=10,k=40,T=15,U_inf=[1,11]).
- T15 (R2E8): exactly three a_i with middle residue (others residue 1 or r-1), r>=4: if r<=30 and nm<=37 (nm = #{a_i == -1 mod r}) then U = [1,B*], B* = T6 - 2*[tau_s<=-2 and s>=2mu], tau = (1-q)prod[rho_i]_q reduced mod q^r-1, mu = largest j in [1,r-1] with tau_j>0, s = (D+1) mod r. (Numerically 0 errors far beyond, incl. r up to 200 and nm>37.)
- Round-2 synthesis (proof refereed, ACCEPT), file /tmp/claude-0/qu/synth/r2/proof.txt (you MAY read this file): with delta = (1-q)A, a 'class pair' is 0<C<r with C == D+1 (mod 2); points x_n = (D+1-Z_n)/2, Z_n = C, 2r-C, 2r+C, 4r-C, ...; y_n = delta_{x_n}; A_n = y_0-y_1+...+(-1)^n y_n; a_n = (-1)^n A_n; n*(C) = least n with a_n<0; N* = min_C n*(C). Thm 3.1: P_b unimodal iff for every class pair the pair condition holds. Thm 4.2: if r divides no a_i, N* == F+1 (mod 2) and U = [1,N*] u {N*+2,...,beta}, beta = min_C beta_C, beta_C = largest b == F+1 with a_{b'-2}+y_{b'} >= 0 for all b' == F+1, b'<=b; N*+1 not in U; N*+2 in U iff |a_{N*}| <= y_{N*+2} for every pair with n*(C)=N*. Thm 4.7 window-centre dichotomy. S2 <=> beta <= N*+2.
- REFUTED (round-2 synthesis, exact, two implementations): the class-pair-LOCAL statement 'beta_C <= n*(C)+2 for every pair C' (this contains (Z2) of the structure-theorem route and the per-thread inequality L'). Counterexample r=8595, k=127, a_i in [1687,1693] (file /tmp/claude-0/qu/synth/r2/inst_ki_fail_r8595.txt): pair C=8594 has n*=3, beta_C=7, yet global U={1,2,3,5}. More: r=12552, r=15167 (F odd), r=50000. Pair-local failures in 42/1822 random instances with r in [2035,79838]; S2 itself held in all. Data for r<=400: no pair-local failure (hill-climb min ratio 1.02 at r=400). So any proof of S2 must combine different class pairs.
- A fast exact C implementation of the class-pair test exists: /tmp/claude-0/qu/synth/r2/c/ (s2check.c; read it, you may compile your own copy in your folder).
- OPEN: Conjecture S2 (only the odd shift b -> b-3 remains: B_off >= B*-3).
box: you may compute P (or anything derived from specific parameter values) ONLY in this region: (i) r<=120, k<=140, every a_i<=400, EXCLUDING (a) instances with exactly 4 or 5 middle residues (a_i mod r in [2,r-2]) whose other parts all have residue 1 or r-1, when k>=20; (b) instances with more than 50 parts of residue r-1, when k>=55; (c) instances whose parts take only two distinct values, both with middle residue, when k>=60; or (ii) r>=1000 (any k, any a_i). Everything with 121<=r<=999 is forbidden. For instances whose coefficients exceed 2^127 use the exact big-integer checker /tmp/claude-0/qu/tools/gt_big.py (profile(r,a,bs) -> list of bools) or your own exact implementation

paths.title: Default: prove the three-middle closed form T15 for ALL r>=4 and ALL nm (remove r<=30, nm<=37).
paths.instructions: T15's upper bound and residue reduction are general; the gap is the lower bound for the base family (m1,m2,m3,(r-1)^nm) when nm>=38 or r>=31. Find a structural argument (e.g. a peeling identity removing pairs of (r-1) factors, or an explicit formula for tau and the pair conditions in this family as functions of nm and r). Prove, or report FAILED with numbers.

paths.title: Alternative: exactly FOUR middle residues: find a closed form for U (in terms of r, Gamma/tau, D, F and a bounded correction), or prove that no Gamma-level closed form exists.
paths.instructions: Work only inside your box (note the exclusion (a): with exactly 4 middle residues and all other residues 1 or r-1 you may use k<=19 only; with other residues present any k<=140). State a candidate rule with free-parameter count, or a non-existence statement with a witness pair (same Gamma-level data, different U). Report all candidates tried.

paths.title: Alternative: the SHARP stabilization threshold L0 (least L such that a_min >= L forces U = [1,F] u (F+U_inf)).
paths.instructions: Either find an explicit formula for the sharp L0 (in terms of r, residues, k), or prove that it is NOT a function of the residue vector alone (exhibit two instances with the same residue vector and same a_min whose stabilization differs, with proof). Report candidates tried and numbers.

paths.title: Alternative: fine structure of the excess E(k) = B*-1-F along families with fixed r and fixed residue proportions: is E(k) - (c k - kappa ln k) eventually periodic / finite-state in k, or genuinely irregular?
paths.instructions: Use exact computation (stay inside your box: r<=120, k<=140, or r>=1000) with large parts (stabilized regime) and the residue-only criterion. Test eventual periodicity, finite-automaton descriptions, or a closed form for the O(1) term; or give evidence/proof of irregularity. Report rule files with fit range and free parameters, or FAILED with numbers.
